clue.text: Writer in Zambia enthralled by climbing plant and tree

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive by, so the Zambia letter sits inside the other letters
climbing in a down clue means going upwards, so the plant and tree are read from the bottom up

parts.note: the aloe is a succulent plant
the lime (linden) is a tree
Z is the international vehicle code for Zambia

explanation.surface: An author in Zambia is captivated by a creeper and a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns the plant and tree together, so the tree comes first in the answer; 'enthralled by' sets Zambia's Z inside that run.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist Zola, author of Germinal and of the open letter J'accuse, is the writer meant.

clue.text: Sign outside front of inn, right over window

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the whole assembly is turned upside down, read bottom to top
outside says the zodiac sign goes round the other letters

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: the front of the word inn is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pub sign hangs outside the inn's front, just over the right-hand window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts I and R inside LEO for LEIRO, and 'over' turns that whole run round.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a bay window that juts out from an upper storey.

clue.text: Preserve a large waterway

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: Keeping a big waterway in good order.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a man-made channel for boats, an artificial waterway.

clue.text: Upset by actions showing inflexibility

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Being upset by what someone does reveals a stubborn streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' only links the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinacy is stubbornness, a refusal to bend or change one's mind.

clue.text: Unsentimental film in which we see bait used on coaster?

indicators.note: in which we see says the film word holds the other letters

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

indicators.note: used on in a down clue places the teasing word above the word for coaster

parts.note: to bait someone is to tease or rag them
a coaster is a small mat for a glass

explanation.surface: A film shows fishing bait spread over a drinks coaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bait' looks like worms for fishing, but it is the verb to tease, RAG; 'coaster' is the drinks mat, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Pragmatic means practical and realistic, guided by results rather than feelings.

clue.text: One living abroad, getting cross, breaking band up

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the cross goes into the middle of the reversed band
up in a down clue says the word for band is read from the bottom

parts.note: tape is a narrow band or strip
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: An emigrant, angry, breaks up a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TAPE into EPAT, and 'breaking' drops X inside it. 'cross' reads as angry, but it is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat (expatriate) is someone who has settled in a country other than their own.

clue.text: See teaching about concessions taken up — by meditator, it may be assumed

definitions.text: by meditator, it may be assumed

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold

indicators.note: about says the teaching word goes round the reversed concessions

parts.note: tuition is teaching

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue says the concessions are read upwards

parts.note: sops are small concessions made to placate someone

explanation.surface: Teaching about concessions, assumed by someone deep in meditation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns SOPS into SPOS, which 'about' places inside TUITION after its first two letters. To 'assume' a position is to take it up, so the definition is a fair description.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-legged lotus posture is the classic seated pose for yoga and meditation.

clue.text: Operetta, having failed, resumed after being revamped

indicators.note: revamped means renovated or remade, so the two words' letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A stage show that flopped is put back on after an overhaul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' only joins the definition to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Strauss II's comic opera Die Fledermaus (The Bat) is one of the best-known Viennese operettas.

clue.text: Theory, presented with alternative, in for a bit of 24 tweaking

indicators.note: 'in for' a letter says the word in takes the place of that letter

parts.note: an option is an alternative, one of the choices open to you

indicators.note: a bit of the word tweaking is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's theory gets a little adjusting once another option is offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of tweaking' is T, the first letter; 'in for' it puts IN where the T of OPTION stood. The stray '24' is an OCR mark, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief someone holds, which is what a theory loosely means in everyday speech.

clue.text: Dog that is retreating after 25 biting

parts.note: biting words or a biting wind are sharp

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is' (id est)

explanation.surface: A dog that bites someone then backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns IE into EI, and 'after' places it behind SHARP. The stray '25' is an OCR mark, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The shar-pei is a Chinese breed known for its deeply wrinkled skin.

clue.text: Extraordinary value of layer of eyeball

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at the remarkable worth of part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The uvea is the pigmented middle layer of the eye, and the adjective describes anything belonging to it.

clue.text: Bond back with M in group providing recurring theme

indicators.note: in says the reversed bond and M go inside the word for group

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch of things, as at an auction

indicators.note: back says the word for bond is read in reverse

parts.note: a tie is a bond linking two things
taken as written
providing means if, as in 'providing it rains'

explanation.surface: It sounds like spy-film talk: James Bond back with his boss M in a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' and 'M' summon the spy films, but Bond is just TIE, turned by 'back' to EIT, and M is the bare letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a repeated musical phrase tied to a character or idea, as in Wagner's operas.

clue.text: Devout liberal ignoring commanding officer

indicators.note: ignoring says the officer's letters are left out of the word for liberal

parts.note: liberal can mean generous or plentiful, so copious

explanation.surface: A religious liberal who pays no attention to the commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' reads as a political label next to 'Devout', but here it means plentiful, COPIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Devout and pious both describe someone deeply religious and observant.

clue.text: Last of runners, losing heat, receiving hard education

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word runners
receiving says the word for losing heat takes in the hard letter

parts.note: something losing heat is cooling down
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The final runner, cooling down after the race, gets a tough lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts H into COOLING after its first letter; S, the last of 'runners', goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling is the instruction a child receives at school, so education.

clue.text: Try and cheat in a terrible way, causing anguish

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it

indicators.note: in a terrible way says the word cheat is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Attempting to cheat badly leads only to grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the judge's sense, hearing a case; 'in a terrible way' makes TACHE out of 'cheat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional pain or grief, the same distress anguish names.

clue.text: Good army required to guard island on behalf of queen

indicators.note: required to guard says the word for good must hold the other letters

parts.note: holy can mean good or saintly
pp (per procurationem) is written before a signature to mean on behalf of
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A good army is needed to defend an island for its queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required to guard' puts I and PP inside HOLY after its H; TA goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippolyta was queen of the Amazons in Greek myth, and appears in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Album possibly containing haysseed and tiny plant

indicators.note: containing says the album letters hold the other letters

parts.note: an album may be issued as a CD, so possibly signals an example
a hayseed (the OCR's spelling) is a country bumpkin, a hick
wee is Scots for small or tiny

explanation.surface: A country singer's album with a hillbilly and a tiny plant on the cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haysseed' is the OCR spelling of hayseed. 'containing' puts HICK and WEE between C and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickweed is a small common weed with white starry flowers.

clue.text: Agent stifles exclamation 3 of disgust with sidekick turning careless

indicators.note: stifles means smothers, so the agent's letters close round the rest

parts.note: an agent can be a spy, a secret agent

indicators.note: turning says the exclamation and the sidekick are each read backwards

parts.note: pah is an exclamation of disgust or contempt
a pal is a friend or sidekick

explanation.surface: A secret agent muffles his partner's grunt of disgust and grows careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes LAP of PAL and HAP of PAH; 'stifles' puts LAPHAP between S and PY. The stray '3' is an OCR mark, not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-happy means casual or haphazard, a happy-go-lucky lack of care.

clue.text: Lecture about to be given with screen

parts.note: c (circa) is the abbreviation for about
to screen something is to hide it

explanation.surface: A lecturer is about to speak, with a screen set up for slides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lecture' is a verb here, to scold, not a talk with slides.
explanation.definitionFit: To lecture someone in the sense of telling them off is to scold or rebuke them.

clue.text: Frown, following most of illusion, nothing to be seen — then flag's produced

indicators.note: following places the word for frown after the other pieces
most of says the word for illusion loses its final letter

parts.note: a trick, as a conjuror's, creates an illusion
O looks like zero, nothing
to lour (or lower) is to frown or scowl

explanation.surface: A magician scowls as an illusion mostly fails, then pulls out a flag with a flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of the word for illusion; 'following' puts the frown word last. LOUR, also spelt lower, is a literary word for scowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricolour is a flag of three bands of colour, such as the French or Irish national flag.

clue.text: House at bottom of mountain in a state

indicators.note: at bottom of in a down clue places the house letters below the mountain

parts.note: Mount Ida, in Crete or Turkey, is a famous mountain of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A house at the foot of a mountain somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the north-west.

clue.text: Criticism I would shortly express

parts.note: a rap is a sharp rebuke or criticism, as in a rap over the knuckles
I'd is the shortened form of I would

explanation.surface: A critic says what they would put into words, briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' is an adjective, as in an express train, not the verb it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and express both mean very fast, as a fast train is an express.

clue.text: Claptrap to pass without murmur? On the contrary

indicators.note: without here means outside, one word going round the other
on the contrary reverses the stated order, so the murmur goes outside the pass rather than the reverse

parts.note: a hum is a low murmuring sound
to OK something is to approve or pass it

explanation.surface: Approving claptrap without a murmur of protest; or perhaps the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, 'pass without murmur' would put the pass outside the murmur; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles, so the murmur goes round the pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokum is nonsense or humbug, the empty talk claptrap describes.

clue.text: Pull excerpt from The Avengers

indicators.note: excerpt from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clip from the TV series The Avengers draws viewers in.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts with the last two letters of 'The' and takes the first three of 'Avengers'.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to haul or drag with effort, a hard pull.

clue.text: Dull quality in work by a municipality

parts.note: op (opus) is a musical work
a city is a municipality, a town with its own local government

explanation.surface: A municipality's art commission has turned out rather dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just joins the work to the rest of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity is the property of not letting light through, so a dullness or lack of shine.

clue.text: United, led by old man, securing overdue period of stability

indicators.note: led by places the father group in front of the letter for United
securing means holding fast, so the father's letters close round the word for overdue

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, the old man
something overdue is late
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A football club, run by an old manager, secures a long-awaited spell of calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led by' puts the PA piece ahead of U.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a level stretch after a rise, so a time when things stay steady.

clue.text: Crude cosmetic, endlessly convenient, covering pore over

indicators.note: endlessly says the cosmetic loses its last letter

parts.note: rouge is a red cosmetic for the cheeks

indicators.note: covering says the word for convenient goes round the word for pore over

parts.note: handy means convenient, close at hand
to pore over a book is to read it closely

explanation.surface: A cheap make-up that is always handy for covering skin pores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pore' looks like part of the skin beside 'cosmetic', but 'pore over' is to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough-and-ready means makeshift or roughly done, the sense of crude as unrefined.
